$comment: Regulatory source-of-truth ledger. Every statutory/guideline constant in the codebase has an entry: where it comes from, where it lives in code, when a human last verified it against the official source, and how often it must be re-verified. scripts/regulatory-freshness.cjs (run by npm run checkup and the daily guardian) FAILS when any entry is overdue. When you verify a value against its source, update lastVerified (YYYY-MM-DD). Never change a value without a citation — that is a Correction to the scenario registry.

entries.rule: Deferred/$0-payment student loans qualified at 1% of outstanding balance
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-6-05 (Monthly Debt Obligations)
entries.notes: NC-01 open in the scenarios registry: generated sources claim 0.5% (that is the FHA Handbook 4000.1 figure). Documented IDR payments may be usable per guide — confirm on next verification.

entries.rule: Self-employment/contract income seasoning: 24 months full; 12-24 conditional
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-3.2 (Self-Employment Income)

entries.rule: Single deposits > 50% of monthly qualifying income must be sourced
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-4.2-02 (Depository Accounts); gifts resolved per B3-4.3-04

entries.rule: VA residual income baselines by region/family size (+$80/member above 5, capped at a family of 7); $0.14/sqft maintenance+utilities on gross living area; residual must exceed guideline by 20% when DTI > 41%
entries.citation: VA Pamphlet 26-7, Revised (2019-02-22 chapter revision), Chapter 4, Topic 9 Items 19/43 and Topic 10.b
entries.codeRef: server/services/underwritingNuance.ts VA_RESIDUAL_MATRIX / VA_EXTRA_MEMBER_FAMILY_CAP / VA_UTILITY_RATE_PER_SQFT / VA_CUSHION_MULTIPLIER; server/underwritingEngine.ts VA path (DB matrix VA_RESIDUAL + VA_RESIDUAL_EXTRA_MEMBER scalar)
entries.notes: Verified 2026-07-04 against the official handbook text (full-PDF mirror; VA WARMS now redirects to a JS-only portal): matrix values for the >= $80,000 band match code exactly; family-of-7 cap confirmed via the handbook's own family-of-8 Georgia example ($1,199 - 'The eighth person will not be considered'). A second table exists for loans <= $79,999 (lower figures, +$75/member) - NOT implemented; sub-$80k loans over-require (conservative). Utilities example confirms gross living area excludes unfinished basement.

entries.rule: Reduce the residual income table figure by 5% if the borrower is an active-duty OR retired serviceperson, OR there is a clear indication of continued military-facility benefits near the property (Guard/Reserve retirees, 100%-disabled Veterans and family, Medal of Honor recipients) - conditions are disjunctive
entries.citation: VA Pamphlet 26-7, Revised, Chapter 4, Topic 9, Item 43 'Reducing the Residual Income Figures'
entries.notes: Resolves roadmap #29: the engine's 5% 'commissary discount' IS sourceable, but its && gate under-applied it - handbook conditions are OR, and retired servicepersons qualify. Intake lacks a dedicated retired/facility-benefits field; that signal routes through hasExchangeAccess until one exists.

entries.rule: Estimation model for the tax deduction in VA residual income: fixed 22% (federal + FICA effective) of gross monthly income, pending real income documents
entries.citation: Platform estimation methodology - NOT a VA figure. VA Pamphlet 26-7 Ch. 4, Topic 9, Items 32-34 prescribe estimated Federal/state income tax and Social Security from IRS/state tax tables on documented income
entries.codeRef: server/services/underwritingNuance.ts RESIDUAL_TAX_RATE (shared; server/underwritingEngine.ts imports it - never fork)
entries.notes: Resolves roadmap #29 tax-rate contradiction: the engine's inline 18% was an uncited fork of this estimation model; unified on 22% (the more conservative figure, and the one the reference tests encode). Replace the fixed rate with IRS/state tax-table estimates when real income documents flow (F3 credit / F5 VOIE).

entries.rule: Standard DTI ceiling used for flags/what-if coaching
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY referencing legacy QM 43% (12 CFR §1026.43 Appendix Q, repealed 2021 — replaced by price-based General QM)
entries.notes: REVIEW CANDIDATE: DU approves DTIs up to 50% with compensating factors; the 43% figure is a conservative platform flag threshold, not a current federal cap. Decide whether to align flag threshold with DU 50% or keep conservative.

entries.rule: PMI-removal opportunity alert at 80% LTV
entries.citation: Homeowners Protection Act, 12 U.S.C. §4901 et seq. (borrower-requested cancellation at 80% LTV of original value; automatic termination at 78%)
entries.notes: Alert uses current estimated value (AVM); statutory cancellation right keys off original value — the alert is an opportunity signal, the letter/request path must use HPA terms.

entries.rule: Low-reserves warning threshold (months of PITI post-closing)
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY; Fannie reserve requirements (B3-4.1-01) vary by transaction — formal mapping pending
entries.notes: Foundation scenario note in the registry: research proper per-transaction reserve requirements.

entries.rule: Document freshness window used for aging alerts
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY (stricter than Fannie B1-1-03, which allows credit documents up to 4 months old for most transactions)
entries.notes: Deliberately conservative; being stricter than the guideline is compliant. Review whether 30-day nagging is too aggressive once real borrowers exist.

entries.citation: Regulation Z, 12 CFR §1026.36(e)(3)
entries.notes: Template text is a summary; legal review recommended before real borrowers sign it (roadmap #26).

entries.rule: NO federal ban on medical debt in credit reports or underwriting — the CFPB Reg V medical-debt rule was VACATED; do not re-import it
entries.citation: Cornerstone Credit Union League v. CFPB (E.D. Tex., joint request), vacating 'Prohibition on Creditors and CRAs Concerning Medical Information (Regulation V)'; no appeal filed within the window. Same ruling held FCRA preempts state medical-debt reporting bans, so state bans are legally doubtful.
entries.codeRef: CTO_ROADMAP.md #28 (no engine change — documented so nobody encodes the vacated rule)
entries.notes: Bureau voluntary policies still hold: unpaid medical collections < $500 and all paid medical collections are not reported by Equifax/Experian/TransUnion. The pre-production doctrine's 'Medical Debt DTI exclusion (2026 rule)' claim is FALSE as a federal rule; the real, citable medical carve-outs are agency underwriting policies (see fnma-b3-5.3-09-medical-collections and fha-4000-1-collections-capacity).

entries.rule: GSE payoff policy: medical collection accounts excluded from collection/charge-off payoff limits (never required to be paid at/prior to closing); non-medical limits: 1-unit primary none, 2-4-unit owner-occ + second homes > $5,000 total, investment $250 individual / $1,000 total
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-5.3-09 (DU Credit Report Analysis — Past-Due, Collection and Charge-Off of Non-Mortgage Accounts)
entries.codeRef: CTO_ROADMAP.md #28 (not yet in code — activates with F3 real credit adapter; collections do not exist in the simulated soft pull)
entries.notes: Verified against the live guide page 2026-07-04 (guide edition 06/03/2026). The $5,000 2-4-unit/second-home threshold differs from the older $250/$1,000 rule of thumb — re-confirm the exact threshold table on next verification. Freddie Mac equivalent (Guide 5401.2) not yet verified — do so before building the F3 adapter.

entries.rule: FHA capacity analysis: if aggregate NON-MEDICAL collection balances > $2,000, include 5% of outstanding balance as monthly debt in DTI (or documented payment plan, or payoff); MEDICAL collections excluded entirely from the threshold and the DTI add
entries.citation: HUD Handbook 4000.1, Origination through Post-Closing — Collection Accounts (TOTAL: II.A.4.b.iv; Manual: II.A.5.a.iv)
entries.codeRef: CTO_ROADMAP.md #28 (not yet in code — the engine has no collections-to-DTI path today; must ship WITH the F3 adapter or FHA files will compute DTI wrong in both directions)
entries.notes: Subsection letters within II.A.4.b.iv / II.A.5.a.iv shift between handbook updates - cite the Collection Accounts heading, and pin exact subsections when implementing.

entries.rule: Reg B amended effective 2026-07-21: disparate-impact ('effects test') liability removed from Regulation B; 'discouragement' narrowed to intentional statements; SPCP restrictions added
entries.citation: CFPB final rule, Equal Credit Opportunity Act (Regulation B), 91 FR (2026-04-22), docket 2026-07804
entries.notes: Our four-fifths-rule monitoring in fairLendingAnalysis.ts is RETAINED deliberately as internal risk management: HMDA is unaffected, state fair-lending laws still recognize effects-based claims, and the deterministic-decisioning invariants don't depend on Reg B's effects test. Do not delete the monitoring in response to this rule; revisit framing/copy that cites Reg B disparate-impact as a legal requirement. This is the real 'July 2026 Reg B rule' the pre-production doctrine referenced - it is unrelated to medical debt.

entries.rule: Mortgage trigger leads: CRAs may not furnish prescreened consumer reports on residential-mortgage credit inquiries EXCEPT to (a) a party with the consumer's documented opt-in authorization, (b) the originator of the consumer's current mortgage, (c) its current servicer, or (d) an insured depository/credit union holding a current account for the consumer. We must never purchase trigger leads outside these exceptions.
entries.citation: Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act, Pub. L. 119-36 (H.R. 2808, 119th Cong.), signed 2025-09-05, amending FCRA §604(c) (15 U.S.C. §1681b(c)); effective 180 days after enactment
entries.codeRef: server/routes/leads.ts (first-party intake only: TrustedForm cert + consent IP/UA/timestamp evidence; the platform purchases no leads)
entries.notes: Sources split on 2026-03-04 vs 03-05 as the exact effective day (180-day count from 2025-09-05) - immaterial, months past either way. Compliance posture is structural: all lead acquisition is first-party/organic, so HPPA binds us only if we ever start buying leads - re-check this entry before any paid-lead initiative. GAO report on text-based trigger-lead solicitations due 2026-09.

entries.rule: Maximum allowable DTI for DU-underwritten conventional loans
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-6-02 (Debt-to-Income Ratios): 'For loan casefiles underwritten through DU, the maximum allowable DTI ratio is 50%.' Manual underwriting max is 36%, extendable to 45% with Eligibility Matrix credit/reserve requirements.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONVENTIONAL_STRETCH_DTI (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Verified against the live Selling Guide page 2026-07-04. Our scalar equals the DU ceiling exactly; any value change routes through the guardian/scenario lane.

entries.rule: Baseline DTI ceiling for standard conventional approvals (below-stretch lane)
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - deliberately conservative baseline. Not an agency figure: Selling Guide B3-6-02 (verified 2026-07-04) allows 50% via DU and 36/45% manual; the pre-2021 ATR/QM 43% appendix-Q threshold this echoes was replaced by the price-based General QM rule.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONVENTIONAL_DTI_CAP (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Conservative-only overlay: files between 43 and 50 DTI route to the stretch/compensating-factors lane rather than auto-pass, which can never approve something the guide would deny. Relaxing it is a business decision via the guardian/scenario lane.

entries.rule: Minimum representative credit score for conventional conforming eligibility
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-5.1-01 (General Requirements, Credit Scores): minimum 620 for fixed-rate loans, 640 for ARMs, manually underwritten; DU casefiles have no fixed floor (DU assesses risk factors).
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONVENTIONAL_FICO_FLOOR (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Verified against the live Selling Guide page 2026-07-04. Platform applies 620 across the board: exact match for fixed-rate; conservative for DU casefiles (which have no published floor). If ARM products are ever offered, the floor for ARMs is 640 - revisit then.

entries.rule: Maximum LTV for conventional conforming loans
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - conservative overlay. Selling Guide B2-1.2-01 (verified 2026-07-04) defers numeric LTV maximums to the Eligibility Matrix; standard 1-unit principal-residence max is 95%, with 95.01-97% available only under specific programs the platform deliberately does not offer yet.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONVENTIONAL_LTV_CAP (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Eligibility Matrix PDF is bot-protected (HTTP 403 on 2026-07-04) - the 95/97 split needs a HUMAN verification pass against the downloaded matrix; B2-1.2-01 page itself was fetched and confirms the matrix is the numeric authority. Offering 97% LTV products later is a business decision via the guardian/scenario lane.

entries.rule: Valuation haircut applied to stock/investment assets in pre-underwriting capacity checks
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - strictly-conservative overlay. VERIFIED AGENCY BASELINE (B3-4.3-01, fetched 2026-07-04): Fannie requires NO percentage haircut - most-recent-statement value is used, and for reserves '100% of the value of the assets may be considered'.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts HAIRCUT_STOCK_INVESTMENT (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Counting only 60% of the asset is stricter than the guide, so it can never approve a file the guide would deny - it CAN under-state buying power. Revisit with F3/F4 real asset verification: market-volatility haircuts are a legitimate platform risk choice but should be an explicit product decision, not an assumed agency rule.

entries.rule: Valuation haircut applied to retirement assets in pre-underwriting capacity checks
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - conservative overlay approximating access costs (penalties/taxes) on retirement funds. Formal mapping to Selling Guide B3-4.3-03 (retirement accounts) pending human verification.
entries.codeRef: server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts HAIRCUT_RETIREMENT (DB policy scalar read by server/underwritingEngine.ts)
entries.notes: Same conservative-only property as platform-haircut-stock-60. Verify B3-4.3-03's current documentation/accessibility conditions on the next pass and decide whether the 70% overlay stays as product policy.

entries.rule: FHFA conforming loan limit, one-unit baseline (loans above route to jumbo)
entries.citation: FHFA 2026 conforming loan limit values, one-unit baseline (contiguous US). Documented inline in shared/lendingLimits.ts as the FHFA 2026 figure.
entries.codeRef: shared/lendingLimits.ts CONFORMING_LOAN_LIMIT_2026; server/scripts/seedLendingGrids.ts CONFORMING_LOAN_LIMIT scalar; jumbo boundary BRC-J30 (min 806500.01)
entries.notes: FHFA publishes new limits each November for the following year - the 2027 update is a seed + BRC-J30 boundary change, and prod/dev reseeds must move together (seedMarketPricing is skip-if-exists).

entries.rule: Window for flagging recently opened tradelines as sleeper debt in liability adjustment
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - conservative detection window. Selling Guide B3-6-05 requires ALL monthly debts including recently opened accounts in the DTI; it does not publish a fixed recency window. The 90-day flag window is the platform's own sleeper-debt detection heuristic (roadmap #32 resolution, 2026-07-04).
entries.notes: The flagged lines' payments are already included in adjustedMonthlyDebt either way - the window only controls the newTradelines advisory surface, so it is detection metadata, not a qualification rule. Same pattern as platform-reserves-2-months.

entries.rule: Loan Estimate must be delivered or placed in the mail within 3 business days of receiving the application
entries.citation: 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(1)(iii): 'delivered not later than three business days after the creditor receives the consumer's application' (verified live 2026-07-04)
entries.codeRef: server/services/trid.ts getTridStatus/evaluateTridTrigger + server/services/businessDays.ts addBusinessDays; hard stop tridHardStopError blocks status advancement past an overdue LE
entries.notes: Overdue = end of the due calendar day without leIssuedDate. LO notified + deal activity recorded at trigger. Covered by tests/trid.test.ts.

entries.rule: A TRID 'application' exists when the creditor has the six pieces of information: name, income, SSN, property address, estimated property value, loan amount sought
entries.citation: 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(3): 'the submission of the consumer's name, the consumer's income, the consumer's social security number to obtain a credit report, the property address, an estimate of the value of the property, and the mortgage loan amount sought' (verified live 2026-07-04)
entries.notes: Name treated as satisfied at account creation (under-counting starts the clock late = violation; over-counting starts early = conservative). Loan amount derived from preApprovalAmount or purchasePrice minus downPayment.

entries.rule: Two-tier 'business day' definition: general (days the creditor's offices are open) for the LE-after-application clock; precise (all calendar days except Sundays and 5 USC 6103(a) federal holidays) for the enumerated waiting periods
entries.citation: 12 CFR 1026.2(a)(6), incl. the enumerated precise-definition sections (1026.19(e)(1)(iii)(B), (e)(4)(ii), (f)(1)(ii), rescission, etc.) (verified live 2026-07-04)
entries.codeRef: server/services/businessDays.ts (excludes Saturdays, Sundays, observed federal holidays for ALL counts)
entries.notes: PLATFORM CONVENTION: one calendar (Mon-Fri minus observed holidays) for both tiers. For the LE clock that reflects a brokerage not open Saturdays (general definition); for precise-definition waiting periods the reg COUNTS Saturdays, so excluding them delays earliest-consummation/receipt math — conservative in both directions, never permissive. 5 USC 6103(a) includes Juneteenth — VERIFIED present in businessDays.ts's holiday list (with Sat→Fri/Sun→Mon observance) 2026-07-04.

entries.rule: Consummation waiting periods: on/after the 7th business day after LE delivery/mailing; revised LE within 3 business days of changed-circumstance info and received no later than 4 business days before consummation; CD received no later than 3 business days before consummation
entries.citation: 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(1)(iii)(B), (e)(4)(i), (e)(4)(ii), (f)(1)(ii) (verified live 2026-07-04: CFPB interactive reg + Cornell LII)
entries.codeRef: server/services/businessDays.ts (documented in header); scheduling NOT yet implemented
entries.notes: Implementation deliberately deferred with triggers: revised-LE windows bind when changed-circumstance repricing ships; CD/consummation scheduling binds when closings are coordinated through the platform. Recorded so the freshness loop keeps the values verified before those features start.

entries.rule: Angel Oak bank-statement qualifying income uses a default expense factor of 50% against eligible deposits
entries.citation: Angel Oak Mortgage Solutions — Bank Statement program page (public)
entries.notes: Lender program parameter (contractual, not regulatory) tracked here because it drives a qualifying-income figure. Transcription: docs/lender-programs/angel-oak/bank-statement-program-reference.md. TPO portal matrix controls on conflict.

entries.rule: Industries with traditionally higher expense factors are underwritten at a 70% expense factor; a factor below 50% requires a third-party CPA/tax-preparer/bookkeeper statement
entries.citation: Angel Oak Mortgage Solutions — Bank Statement program page (public)
entries.notes: Transcription: docs/lender-programs/angel-oak/bank-statement-program-reference.md.

entries.rule: Angel Oak Investor Cash Flow DSCR = expected rent divided by PITIA (principal, interest, taxes, insurance, HOA) — 'Rent Divided PITIA = DSCR'
entries.citation: Angel Oak Mortgage Solutions — DSCR loan calculator page (public, operative formula)
entries.notes: Qualifying MINIMUM by tier is portal-gated and deliberately absent from code; the path reports the ratio and flags manual review. Transcription: docs/lender-programs/angel-oak/dscr-program-reference.md.

entries.rule: Reg Z advertising: (d)(1) triggering terms = (i) amount/percentage of any downpayment, (ii) number of payments or period of repayment, (iii) amount of any payment, (iv) amount of any finance charge; when any is stated, (d)(2) requires stating (i) the downpayment amount/%, (ii) the terms of repayment over the full term incl. any balloon, and (iii) the 'annual percentage rate' using that term, and if the rate may increase after consummation, that fact
entries.citation: Regulation Z, 12 CFR §1026.24(d)(1)-(2) (verified verbatim via eCFR API 2026-07-11)
entries.notes: LO-5 comms lint. Deterministic lexicon, NOT NLP (I1). Enforcement = BLOCK a free-text send stating a specific rate/payment/downpayment figure and route to the Loan Estimate / LO-3 Advisor Report, because (d)(2)(iii) requires the borrower-specific APR which a generic appended block cannot supply; blocking is stricter than the rule and therefore compliant. SCOPING (compliance sign-off item): a bare product period like '30-year fixed' is intentionally NOT a standalone trigger — the (d)(1)(ii) leg fires only on an explicit payment COUNT ('360 payments'). The disclosure block is the reference text the disclosed channels carry, not appended to messages.

entries.rule: Reg N (MAP Rule) prohibits material misrepresentations in commercial communications about any mortgage term, including the interest rate / whether 'fixed', the existence/nature/amount of fees or costs, payment amounts, whether the consumer has been or will be approved ('preapproved or guaranteed'), and government affiliation/endorsement
entries.value: promise-phrase -> warn+rewrite lexicon v1 (Tier 2, WARN not block)
entries.citation: Regulation N, 12 CFR §1014.3 (MAP Rule; verified verbatim via eCFR API 2026-07-11)
entries.notes: LO-5 comms lint Tier 2. Deterministic lexicon, NOT NLP (I1). WARN-not-block: flags guaranteed/assured approval, superlative rate claims, no-fees, and false government affiliation, each with a compliant rewrite; a send-anyway is an override the server audit-logs. Subsection letters in the per-rule citations are approximate to the eCFR enumeration and are a compliance sign-off item.

entries.rule: Anti-steering safe-harbor loan options per type of transaction: (A) the loan with the lowest interest rate; (B) the loan with the lowest interest rate without negative amortization, a prepayment penalty, interest-only payments, a balloon payment in the first 7 years of the life of the loan, a demand feature, shared equity, or shared appreciation; (C) the loan with the lowest total dollar amount of discount points, origination points or origination fees (ties broken by the lowest interest rate among them); originator must have a good faith belief the options are loans for which the consumer likely qualifies (e)(3)(ii)
entries.citation: Regulation Z, 12 CFR §1026.36(e)(2)-(3) (verified verbatim via eCFR API 2026-07-11)
entries.notes: Option-set DERIVATION for the LO-2 scenario simulator; the borrower-facing disclosure template is the separate regz-1026-36e-anti-steering entry (consentGate.ts). (e)(3)(ii) good-faith qualification is satisfied structurally: the simulator runs deterministic qualification per offer. Catalog carries no prepayment-penalty/demand/shared-equity flags; the (B) leg derives risky features from amortizationType markers (IO/balloon/neg-am) — the PPE adapter must map real feature flags when the contract lands.

entries.rule: Non-subject rental property DTI treatment: monthly qualifying rental income (75% of gross rent) minus full PITIA — positive result added to total monthly income, negative result added to total monthly obligations; PITIA never separately double-counted
entries.value: positive → income; negative → obligations; 75% factor; PITIA inside the net only
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-3.8-01 Rental Income (10/08/2025) — formerly B3-3.1-08 before the Income Assessment reorganization. Verbatim: 'If the monthly qualifying rental income minus the full PITIA is positive, it must be added to the borrower's total monthly income'; 'If the monthly qualifying rental income minus PITIA is negative, the monthly net rental loss must be added to the borrower's total monthly obligations.'
entries.codeRef: server/services/income/paths/rental.ts (net offset), server/services/income/orchestrator.ts (income-side application), server/services/decisionEngine.ts (obligation-side application); transcription docs/fannie-mae/rental-income-reference.md
entries.notes: DTI application shipped with the Phase-1 rental wiring (non-W2 plan §3.1); previously computed advisory-only.

entries.rule: Subject-property 2-4 unit principal residence: qualifying rental income from the non-occupied unit(s) is ADDED to total monthly income while the FULL subject PITIA remains in total monthly obligations — never netted
entries.value: income-side only; full PITIA stays in housing expense
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-3.8-01 Rental Income (10/08/2025) — formerly B3-3.1-08. Verbatim: 'the full amount of the mortgage payment (PITIA) must be included in the borrower's total monthly obligations.' Netting qualifying rent against subject PITIA in the applied math would double-count the PITIA already carried in the housing expense.
entries.codeRef: server/services/income/orchestrator.ts subjectPropertyRental application; advisory display remains calculateSubjectPropertyRentalOffset (server/services/underwritingNuance.ts)
entries.notes: S-06 upgraded from advisory to applied income-side; the borrower-facing flag now reports the income-side figure.

entries.rule: WHEN rental offsets auto-apply: positive net rental income applies only at decision-grade financialDataProvenance (verified income/assets/credit); negative net rental applies to obligations ALWAYS, including PRELIMINARY decisions
entries.value: positive gated on verification; negative always counted
entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY - strictly-conservative overlay. VERIFIED AGENCY BASELINE (B3-3.8-01, fetched 2026-07-17): the guide states the arithmetic and documentation (Schedule E / leases + 2 months of receipt evidence / Form 1007-1025) but not an automation gate; applying declared-but-unverified positive rent to a preliminary decision could over-state qualification, so the platform withholds it until provenance is decision-grade. Counting a declared loss early can only under-state.
entries.codeRef: server/services/income/orchestrator.ts (applyRentalToDti gate from shared/dataProvenance.ts isDecisionGrade), server/services/income/paths/rental.ts
entries.notes: Asymmetry can never approve a file the guide would deny. Includes the mortgage-liability coexistence guard: applied offsets alongside mortgage-type URLA liability rows flag manual review instead of silently risking a PITIA double-count.

entries.rule: Partnership/LLC (Form 1065) entity cash-flow analysis: add back depreciation, depletion, amortization, casualty and other non-recurring losses; subtract the travel & meals exclusion, non-recurring income, and mortgages/notes/bonds payable in less than one year (waived when they roll over regularly and/or liquid assets cover them); borrower share per the K-1 percentage of Ending Capital; usable only with distributions consistent with the income used or adequate business liquidity
entries.value: named-category add-backs/subtractions × ownership share, distributions-or-liquidity gated
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-3.7-01, Analyzing Partnership Returns for a Partnership or LLC (02/07/2024). Fetched live 2026-07-17; transcription in docs/fannie-mae/self-employment-income-reference.md §Business returns.
entries.codeRef: server/services/selfEmploymentIncome.ts K-1 lane entityShare; shared/schema/lendingUrla.ts entityCashFlowAnalysisSchema
entries.notes: The guide names no IRS line numbers; the worksheet collects by named category. Missing ownership percentage skips the adjustment and flags review — never guessed.

entries.rule: S corporation (Form 1120-S) entity cash-flow analysis: same add-back/subtraction taxonomy as B3-3.7-01; borrower share per the K-1 percentage of stock ownership; owner W-2 wages are income 'in addition to their proportionate share' and count directly (in this codebase inside the K-1 lane, since the agency wage path skips self-employed employment rows)
entries.value: entity adjustments × stock-ownership share, distributions-or-liquidity gated; owner W-2 direct
entries.citation: Fannie Mae Selling Guide B3-3.7-02, Analyzing Returns for an S Corporation (02/07/2024). Verbatim: owners 'may receive income in the form of wages or dividends in addition to their proportionate share of business income (or loss) reported on Schedule K-1.' Fetched live 2026-07-17; transcription in docs/fannie-mae/self-employment-income-reference.md §Business returns.
entries.codeRef: server/services/selfEmploymentIncome.ts K-1 lane (entityShare + w2FromBusiness direct); shared/schema/lendingUrla.ts k1 worksheet
entries.notes: Resolves the reference doc's former open question on owner W-2 treatment. No double-count: computeAgencyWageIncome skips isSelfEmployed employment rows by design.

entries.rule: S-07 departing-residence conversion: the offset runs on PROJECTED market rent, so any evaluation including a departing residence carries requiresManualReview until a rental appraisal (Form 1007) or executed lease plus the most recent Schedule E (newly-placed-in-service confirmation) is verified; the departing residence never enters the DSCR portfolio view

entries.notes: VERIFIED VERBATIM 2026-08-20 against docs/reg-z/12-cfr-1026-regulation-z.xml (eCFR full Part 1026 + Supplement I, Title 12 latest_amended_on 2026-08-06, up_to_date_as_of 2026-08-18, captured 2026-08-20). 1026.36(d)(2)(i)(A): if any loan originator receives compensation directly from a consumer, (1) no loan originator shall receive compensation, directly or indirectly, from any person other than the consumer in connection with the transaction, and (2) no person who knows or has reason to know of the consumer-paid compensation shall pay any compensation to a loan originator. The implementation (borrowerPaidOriginationAllowed => model === 'borrower_paid'; the fee is ZERO, not merely disclosed differently, under lender_paid) is consistent with that text. Supp. I comment 36(d)(2)(i)-1 confirms the restriction reaches payments 'whether before, at, or after consummation', and confirms a creditor MAY still provide funds for the consumer's benefit so long as they are applied solely to costs other than loan originator compensation. TWO NUANCES NOW NAMED, neither currently reachable in the product: (a) 1026.36(d)(2)(i)(B) treats funds provided under an agreement between the consumer and a non-creditor third party toward the consumer's costs as CONSUMER-paid — the platform models no such agreements, and if one is ever added it must route to borrower_paid; (b) 1026.36(d)(2)(i)(C) permits a loan originator ORGANIZATION paid by the consumer to compensate its individual originator, which is internal comp and does not touch this borrower-fee gate. The prior 'network blocked' note is superseded: ecfr.gov answered 200 with genuine section text on 2026-08-20 and the copy is now captured locally.

entries.notes: COMPOSITION VERIFIED VERBATIM 2026-08-20 against docs/reg-z/12-cfr-1026-regulation-z.xml (eCFR full Part 1026 + Supplement I, Title 12 latest_amended_on 2026-08-06, up_to_date_as_of 2026-08-18, captured 2026-08-20). 1026.32(b)(1)(ii) includes all compensation paid directly or indirectly by a consumer or creditor to a loan originator, attributable to the transaction at the time the rate is set, EXCEPT (A) consumer-to-broker compensation already counted under (b)(1)(i), (B) broker-to-its-own-employee, (C) creditor-to-its-own-employee, and (D) manufactured-home retailer-to-employee. This CONFIRMS the module's central claim: Homiquity is a BROKER, not the creditor's employee, so exception (C) does not reach it and creditor-paid compensation IS included — the lender-paid model makes the QM cap harder to satisfy, not easier. Exception (A) is the double-count rule that pointsAndFeesFloor's borrowerPaidDouble handling already mirrors. THE FLOOR REMAINS A DELIBERATE LOWER BOUND and its notes are unchanged on that point: (b)(1)(i) pulls in the entire 1026.4(a)/(b) finance charge less six exclusions (including bona fide third-party charges not retained by creditor/originator/affiliate, and up to two bona fide discount points), and (iii)-(vi) add 1026.4(c)(7) items, credit insurance premiums and prepayment penalties — none of which this platform computes. Over-cap verdicts stay sound by monotonicity; under-cap is still reported 'not cleared', never compliant. Promoting the floor to an authoritative Regulation Z figure is now UNBLOCKED by this capture, but it is code work, not a verification — do not treat this entry as authorising it. Related open item unchanged: whether lender-paid broker compensation is a finance charge under 1026.4(a)(3) (see regz-1026-4-platform-finance-charge-classification).

entries.rule: Good-faith fee tolerance tiers: ZERO tolerance for charges paid to the creditor/loan originator/affiliate, services the consumer cannot shop for, and transfer taxes; TEN PERCENT cumulative for recording fees and shoppable services taken from the creditor's written provider list; NO numeric tolerance for prepaid interest, insurance premiums and escrow deposits. Baselines reset only on a valid changed circumstance.
entries.citation: Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.19(e)(3)(i)-(iv) (VERIFIED); refund per 1026.19(f)(2)(v)
entries.notes: TIER COMPOSITION VERIFIED VERBATIM 2026-08-20 against docs/reg-z/12-cfr-1026-regulation-z.xml (eCFR full Part 1026 + Supplement I, Title 12 latest_amended_on 2026-08-06, up_to_date_as_of 2026-08-18, captured 2026-08-20). (e)(3)(i) is a general rule — an estimate is in good faith if the charge does not exceed the amount disclosed, EXCEPT as provided in (ii)-(iv) — so zero tolerance is the RESIDUAL bucket, which is how the module treats it. (e)(3)(ii) gives the 10 percent AGGREGATE to 'a charge for a third-party service or a recording fee', conditioned on (B) the third-party charge not being paid to the creditor or an affiliate and (C) the creditor permitting the consumer to shop consistent with (e)(1)(vi). (e)(3)(iii) gives no numeric tolerance to (A) prepaid interest, (B) property insurance premiums, (C) escrow/impound/reserve amounts, (D) consumer-selected providers NOT on the creditor's written list, and (E) property taxes and other charges for third-party services not required by the creditor. CLASSIFICATION CHOICE 1 IS NOW CONFIRMED CORRECT, not merely conservative: with no written provider list feature, (e)(1)(vi)(C) cannot be satisfied, so (ii)(C) fails and shoppable services fall to the (i) residual — zero tolerance, as implemented. Recording fees take the 10 percent aggregate without the shopping condition, as implemented. Transfer taxes appear in neither (ii) nor (iii), so they are residual zero, as implemented — note (iii)(E) says PROPERTY taxes, a different LE line. ONE REFINEMENT FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED: (e)(3)(iii)(E) places property taxes in the no-numeric-tolerance bucket; this module classifies them zero-tolerance. That is STRICTER than the rule requires, so it cannot create the violation it guards against — but reclassifying them would LOOSEN a disclosure gate, which is a founder decision, never a verification outcome. Left as-is and recorded here. Unchanged: this module raises a redisclosure gate and an exposure figure; it does not decide a legal cure.

Vendor pass-throughs (tax service) are never discounted. Compensation alone exceeding the cap is not rescued - the file stays non-originable and the gates refuse it.

entries.citation: PLATFORM POLICY resolving audit F-17. Charging a consumer LESS than a disclosed-schedule amount is permitted and requires no changed circumstance; the constraint being fitted is 12 CFR 1026.43(e)(2)(iii) via the Loan Delivery QM Edits Job Aid tiers.
entries.notes: DOCTRINE CHANGE - NEEDS COUNSEL. Opened 2026-08-05 resolving F-17, the non-QM dead band created by a fixed fee meeting a tiered cap. The fix removes the fixedness rather than picking a different fixed number, so the band cannot reappear when the CFPB adjusts the 1026.43(e) dollar amounts annually. TWO THINGS A HUMAN MUST CONFIRM. (1) It NARROWS an earlier invariant. The F-1 remediation asserted that borrower-facing totals are wholly invariant to lender-paid compensation, because the Loan Estimate has no paid-by-others column. That is no longer literally true: comp and our fees consume the same cap, so a richer comp plan now yields a smaller borrower fee. Compensation is still never ADDED to any borrower total, and the surviving invariant is directional - more compensation can never increase a borrower charge - which is pinned by tests/loCompensation.test.ts. Economically this is a lender credit, and it always runs in the borrower's favour, but whether a fee that varies with the comp plan is acceptable disclosure practice is a counsel question, not an engineering one. (2) Fair-lending posture: the reduction is formulaic and driven only by loan amount and comp plan, never discretionary and never by borrower characteristic. That is the safest form, but it should be confirmed as part of the fair-lending review since loan amount correlates with other things. Reset reviewIntervalDays to 180 once both are cleared.

entries.notes: OPENED BY THE 2026-08-08 FINANCIAL ARCHITECTURE AUDIT (F-21). This is NOT a verified reading - it is an unverified posture recorded so it cannot be forgotten. WHAT WAS VERIFIED, IN CODE: (1) the payout path is live and admin-gated, and its rate is chosen per file rather than set by a fixed schedule; (2) the rate is applied to the LOAN AMOUNT with no server-side check against the compensation expected or received on that file, so the permitted maximum of 10% on a $250,000 loan creates a $25,000 payable against roughly $5,000 of revenue at the seeded 200 bps lender-paid plan; (3) calculateAgentCommission has zero callers today, and its referrer gate tests for a role string 'agent' that does not exist in shared/roles.ts ALL_ROLES - so only role 'broker' could ever satisfy it, and the realtor and cpa partner personas cannot. That is the RESPA-safe posture, but it reads as incidental rather than designed; (4) CTO_ROADMAP.md item 3.7 schedules wiring that function to the funded-loan transition, at which point the payout becomes 25% of a lender compensation figure that varies by lender and product. TWO QUESTIONS FOR COUNSEL BEFORE EITHER PATH CARRIES A LIVE FILE. (a) Is a per-file discretionary percentage of the loan amount a 'fixed percentage of the amount of credit extended' under 1026.36(d)(1)(ii), or is it compensation that varies by transaction? The 25%-of-lender-comp variant is the sharper case, since lender comp bps differ by lender and product. (b) If the payee is a referral source rather than a loan originator, does the payment survive RESPA section 8? The partner tables (shared/schema/partners.ts, shared/schema/cpaPartners.ts) were deliberately built with NO fee or commission columns for exactly this reason (charter 5-C1), and broker_commissions is that column set sitting on the same referral edge. WHY IT CANNOT BE ANSWERED HERE: Reg Z cannot be verified from inside a session - ecfr.gov, consumerfinance.gov, govinfo.gov and law.cornell.edu are all blocked, and docs/reg-z/ holds no source text. Reg X is likewise absent from docs/. The 14-day interval is deliberate so this goes loud until answered; reset to 180 once counsel clears both questions. || CORRECTION 2026-08-20: the 'every regulatory host is blocked' condition recorded above was true when written and is NOW FALSE — ecfr.gov answered HTTP 200 with genuine section text (verified by grepping the body, not the status code), and the full 12 CFR Part 1026 + Supplement I is captured at docs/reg-z/12-cfr-1026-regulation-z.xml.
